speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; tell me, did these symptoms start simultaneously or did the rash appear after you felt unwell?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola). The history of fever, rhinorrhea, headache followed by a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, specifically with a facial rash appearing 4 days after onset and sparing the perioral area, is highly characteristic of the maculopapular rash progression seen in measles.
